notes: The costs verdict on Today's picks now judges each share by the costs these picks actually pay: $6 round-trip brokerage — because the picks buy with a limit order (you never pay the buy–sell gap) and sell at the next morning's opening auction. That's the same cost model the decade backtest was proven under. The market spread still shows, but as context: it's what buying at market WOULD add, and the limit entry exists to avoid it. Each share is judged on its own numbers — a real edge on a proper parcel now reads green, and only genuinely uneconomic trades are called out. The server applies the identical test, so the app and the picks it receives can never disagree.
